--global variable so local ?
---[[
print(10)         --> 10
--]]
-- nil, boolean, number, string, userdata, function, thread, and table
--Conditionals (such as the ones in control structures) consider false and nil as false
	and anything else as tru
--print(10 .. 20)        --> 1020
---[[    a = {}     -- create a table and store its reference in `a'
    k = "x"
    a[k] = 10        -- new entry, with key="x" and value=10
--]]
A common mistake for beginners is to confuse a.x with a[x].
	The first form represents a["x"], that is, a table indexed by the string "x".
	The second form is a table indexed by the value of the variable x.
-- read 10 lines storing them in a table
	a = {}
	for i=1,10 do
		a[i] = io.read()
	end
For instance, you could print the lines read in the last example with the following code:
	for i,line in ipairs(a) do
		print(line)
	end
--x = x or v
--(a and b) or c (or simply a and b or c) in C is  a ? b : c
